mainTopic: The dispute between אביי and רבא about doing a forbidden act on שבת without intending its forbidden form, followed by the משנה listing the 39 אבות מלאכות.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a proof for רבא from a ברייתא that contrasts שבת with שאר מצות. The proof reads the ברייתא as saying that one who meant to cut a detached plant but cut an attached one is פטור on שבת. אביי answers that the ברייתא is talking about one who meant only to lift the plant, and in that case even he agrees the person is פטור. The גמרא then brings two more cases where אביי and רבא argue the same way: meaning to throw two אמות and throwing four, and throwing in what he thought was a רשות היחיד that turned out to be a רשות הרבים. It explains why all three cases are needed. Next it challenges רבא from רבי יוחנן's rule that one who does all 39 מלאכות in one lapse of awareness is liable for each: how can someone know it is שבת yet be unaware of the מלאכות? The answer is that he knew the לאו but not the כרת (per רבי יוחנן), or he knew only the Torah law of תחומין (per ריש לקיש and רבי עקיבא). Finally a new משנה lists all 39 אבות מלאכות: bread-making, cloth-making, leather-making, and a closing group ending with carrying between domains.

steps.title: The ברייתא's two halves refer to different comparisons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the first half of the ברייתא compares שבת to עבודה זרה, and the second half compares שבת to שאר מצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must it not be that the first part deals with עבודה זרה and the last part deals with other מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles how to read a ברייתא it has been analyzing. This is a setup: once this reading is fixed, the next step uses it to prove רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists ways שבת is stricter and ways it is more lenient. Earlier attempts to read both halves as one comparison did not work. So the גמרא splits them: the רישא contrasts שבת with עבודה זרה, and the סיפא contrasts שבת with שאר מצות.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the forced conclusion)
The first clause of a teaching
The last clause of a teaching
Other מצוות (besides the one being discussed)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that the first clause is about idolatry,
and the last clause is about other מצוות?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, רֵישָׁא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְסֵיפָא בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the analysis of the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's סיפא compares שבת with שאר מצות, and that comparison will be used next.

steps.title: Proof for רבא: cutting an attached plant by mistake is exempt on שבת
steps.stepSummary: With שאר מצות, 'unwitting without intent' means eating חלב while thinking it is permitted שומן, and he is liable. On שבת, by contrast, one who meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one is פטור, just as רבא says.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'unwitting without intent' in other מצוות? He thought it was permitted fat and ate it. That is not so on שבת, where he is exempt: one who intended to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the reading from step 1 to prove רבא's view. The ברייתא says that on שבת this kind of mistake is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For other מצוות, the act he intended (eating) is exactly the act that is forbidden, so he is liable. On שבת he intended to cut something detached, which is not a מלאכה at all. The ברייתא calls this פטור, which matches רבא and challenges אביי, who holds him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinned unwittingly without intending the forbidden act
Permitted fat (as opposed to forbidden חֵלֶב)
What is the case? How do we picture it?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this person is innocent in other מצוות too. For שאר מצות he IS liable. Only on שבת does the ברייתא say פטור, because שבת requires מלאכת מחשבת, meaning intentional, thought-out work.

phrases.english: And 'unwitting without intent'
regarding other מצוות, what is the case?
Where he thought it was permitted fat, and ate it.
Which is not so on Shabbat, where he is exempt,
as one who intended to cut the detached plant
and cut the attached one is exempt.
phrases.notes: This is exactly the case where אביי and רבא argue; here it fits רבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁגַג בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading established in step 1 to prove רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that one who intended to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one is פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא contrasting שבת with שאר מצות, which says such a person is exempt on שבת.

steps.title: אביי reads the ברייתא with different cases
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'unwitting without intent' in שאר מצות means swallowing חלב while thinking it was saliva. The exempt case on שבת is one who meant only to LIFT a detached plant. But one who meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, what is 'unwitting without intent'? He thought it was saliva and swallowed it. That is not so on שבת, where he is exempt: one who intended to lift a detached plant and cut an attached one is exempt. But one who intended to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. He gives the ברייתא a more extreme set of cases, so it does not contradict him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, 'without intent' means he did not intend the action at all: he did not mean to eat, and he did not mean to cut, only to lift. In that extreme case even אביי agrees he is פטור on שבת. Where he did mean to cut, he performed a real act of cutting, so אביי still holds he is חייב.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that intending to LIFT but cutting by mistake is פטור. The argument is only about intending to CUT something detached but cutting something attached: אביי says חייב, and רבא says פטור.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַבָּיֵי שָׁגַג בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? —
phrases.english: And for Abaye, what is the case of 'unwitting without intent'?
Where he thought it was saliva, and swallowed it.
Which is not so on Shabbat, where he is exempt,
as one who intended to lift the detached plant
and cut the attached one is exempt.
But one who intended to cut the detached plant
and cut the attached one is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי שָׁגַג בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the proof of step 2 by redefining the cases in the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא proves רבא. The ברייתא can fit אביי as well.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא's שבת case is 'intended to cut'. It could instead be 'intended to lift', where even אביי exempts.

steps.title: Second dispute: meant to throw two אמות, threw four
steps.stepSummary: Someone meant to throw an object two אמות in a רשות הרבים, but it went four. רבא says פטור, because he did not intend a four-אמה throw. אביי says חייב, because he did intend a throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who intended to throw two and threw four. רבא said he is exempt; אביי said he is liable. רבא says exempt because he did not intend a throw of four. אביי says liable because he did intend a throw in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another recorded argument between אביי and רבא that follows the same pattern as the cutting case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing four אמות in a רשות הרבים is forbidden, but two אמות is not. רבא looks at the forbidden result, which he never intended. אביי looks at the action, a throw, which he did intend, so he is liable for what actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: A throw in general, without regard to distance
Four אמות, the forbidden distance in a רשות הרבים

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר: נִתְכַּוֵּון לִזְרוֹק שְׁתַּיִם וְזָרַק אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: It was stated: one who intended to throw two cubits and threw four,

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: פָּטוּר. אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: Rava said: exempt. Abaye said: liable.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר פָּטוּר — דְּלָא קָמִיכַּוֵּין לִזְרִיקָה דְאַרְבַּע.
phrases.english: Rava said exempt, because he did not intend a throw of four.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אֲמַר חַיָּיב — דְּהָא קָמִיכַּוֵּין לִזְרִיקָה בְּעָלְמָא.
phrases.english: Abaye said liable, because he did intend a throw in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: נִתְכַּוֵּון לִזְרוֹק שְׁתַּיִם וְזָרַק אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case of the same מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intending two אמות but throwing four: רבא says פטור, and אביי says חייב.

steps.title: Third dispute: thought it was a private domain
steps.stepSummary: Someone threw four אמות thinking he was in a רשות היחיד, but it turned out to be a רשות הרבים. רבא says פטור, since he did not intend a forbidden throw. אביי says חייב, since he intended a throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he thought it was a private domain and it turned out to be a public domain: רבא says exempt, and אביי says liable. רבא says exempt because he did not intend a forbidden throw. אביי says liable because he did intend a throw in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third case of the same dispute, this time about a mistake about the place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a רשות היחיד, throwing any distance is permitted. So the person here intended a fully permitted act. רבא exempts him for lacking a forbidden intent, while אביי again focuses on the intended throw.

phrases.aramaic: כְּסָבוּר רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, וְנִמְצֵאת רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים —
phrases.english: If he thought it was a private domain, and it turned out to be a public domain,

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: פָּטוּר, וְאַבָּיֵי אָמַר: חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: Rava said: exempt, and Abaye said: liable.
Rava said exempt,
because he did not intend a forbidden throw.
And Abaye said liable,
because he did intend a throw in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּסָבוּר רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, וְנִמְצֵאת רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thinking it was a רשות היחיד when it was a רשות הרבים: רבא says פטור, and אביי says חייב.

steps.title: Why the throwing case is needed after the cutting case
steps.stepSummary: From the cutting case alone, we might think רבא exempts only because the intended act was not forbidden at all. In the throwing case, four אמות cannot happen without the first two, so we might think רבא agrees with אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary: had it taught us only the first case, we would say רבא exempts there because he did not intend a forbidden cutting. But one who intended two and threw four, where four cannot be thrown without the two, we might say רבא agrees with אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it needed to record all three disputes. It starts with why the throwing case adds something beyond the cutting case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cutting case, cutting a detached plant has no forbidden part at all. In the throwing case, the two אמות he intended are actually part of the four-אמה throw. So one could think רבא would hold him liable there. Recording the throwing dispute shows that רבא exempts even then.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to state all the cases)

phrases.english: And it is necessary: for if it had taught us only the first case,
in that case Rava says exempt,
because he did not intend a forbidden cutting.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִתְכַּוֵּון לִזְרוֹק שְׁתַּיִם וְזָרַק אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: But one who intended to throw two and threw four,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַרְבַּע בְּלָא תַּרְתֵּי לָא מִיזְדַּרְקִי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: since four cannot be thrown without the two,
I might say he agrees with Abaye.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The throwing case teaches that רבא exempts even when the intended act is part of the forbidden act.

steps.title: Why the private-domain case is needed after the throwing case
steps.stepSummary: From the throwing case alone, we might think רבא exempts only because he did not intend four אמות. In the private-domain case he did intend four אמות, so we might think רבא agrees with אביי. Therefore all the cases are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And had it taught us only this case, we would say רבא exempts here because he did not intend a throw of four. But where he thought it was a private domain and it turned out to be public, where he did intend a throw of four, I might say רבא agrees with אביי. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why each case is needed. Each case shows רבא's view in a harder situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the private-domain case, he fully intended the forbidden distance of four אמות. His only mistake was about the type of place. Even so, רבא exempts him, because intending a permitted throw is not intending a forbidden one.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, a person is liable on שבת only if he intended a forbidden act. אביי is satisfied if he intended the action itself. The three cases show רבא holding his view in harder and harder situations.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us this case,
in this case Rava says exempt,
because he did not intend a throw of four,
but where he thought it was a private domain
and it turned out to be a public domain,
where he does intend a throw of four,
I might say he agrees with Abaye. Therefore it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three disputes are needed; רבא exempts even when he intended the full forbidden distance.

steps.title: Recalling the count of thirty-nine מלאכות and רבי יוחנן's explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls the משנה, 'אבות מלאכות ארבעים חסר אחת', and the earlier question of why the number is given. רבי יוחנן answered that one who does all of them in one lapse of awareness is liable for each one separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'The main categories of labor are forty less one,' and we discussed it: why do I need the number? And רבי יוחנן said: if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against רבא by bringing an earlier teaching. The attack itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of 39 teaches that each מלאכה brings its own חטאת. This applies to someone who knew it was שבת but did not know these acts were forbidden (זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות). The next step asks how such a case is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The main categories of forbidden labor
Why do I need the number?

phrases.english: We learned: 'The primary labors are forty less one,'
and we discussed it: why do I need the number?
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of attack on רבא's position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing all 39 מלאכות in one lapse of awareness makes one liable for each separately.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא: how can such a case happen?
steps.stepSummary: For אביי, the case is simple: he knew שבת and its מלאכות but erred about the minimum amounts (שיעורין). For רבא, who exempts such mistakes, how can someone know it is שבת yet be unaware of the מלאכות?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for אביי, who says one is liable in a case like this. You find it where he knew the prohibition of שבת and knew the forbidden labors, but erred about the amounts. But for רבא, who says exempt, how do you find a case of knowing it is שבת but being unaware of the labors?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. It asks how רבי יוחנן's case can ever happen according to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's case needs a person who knows it is שבת but is unaware about the מלאכות. For אביי this is easy: he knew the מלאכות were forbidden and only misjudged the שיעור, meaning to do less than the amount that makes one liable. רבא cannot use this case, because for him that mistake is פטור, just like intending two אמות and throwing four. So רבא needs another case.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (one view), setting up a contrast
Being unaware that the acts are forbidden מלאכות
You can find such a case

steps.confusionAlert: The 'בשלמא... אלא' format does not mean אביי is being proven correct. It only shows that אביי has an easy case and that רבא must now find one of his own.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַבָּיֵי דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: It works well for Abaye, who said that in a case like this he is liable,
you find it where he knew the prohibition of Shabbat
and knew the prohibition of the labors,
but erred about the amounts.
But for Rava, who said exempt,
how do you find it
with awareness of Shabbat and unawareness of the labors?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַבָּיֵי דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from step 8 to attack רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one who intends less than the forbidden act (for example, intending to throw two אמות but throwing four) is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's case requires knowing it is שבת while being unaware of the מלאכות. The natural way to picture this, a mistake about שיעורין, is exempt according to רבא, so his view seems to leave no real case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces רבא to give a new definition of זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות. Steps 10 through 12 supply it.

steps.title: Under רבי יוחנן, he knew the לאו but not the כרת
steps.stepSummary: If רבא follows רבי יוחנן, being unaware of כרת is enough to count as שוגג. So the person 'knew שבת' in the sense that he knew there was a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well if רבא holds like רבי יוחנן, who said that once a person was unaware of the כרת, even if he knew about the לאו and did it on purpose, he counts as unaware. Then we find a case where he knew שבת as a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question of Step 9 for רבא, using the opinion of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that if a person did not know the act carries כרת, he is still a שוגג, even if he knew it was forbidden. So 'knowing שבת' means he knew the מלאכות are forbidden by a לאו. 'Unaware of the מלאכות' means he did not know they carry כרת. This way he can be חייב a separate קרבן for each מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (this fits nicely)
Spiritual 'cutting off', the heavenly punishment for deliberate שבת violation
You can find such a case

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'he knew שבת' does NOT mean he only knew what day it was. It means he knew the מלאכות were forbidden by a לאו. What he did not know was that they carry כרת.

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: It works out well if he holds like Rabbi Yochanan,
who said: once he was unaware regarding karet,
even though he acted knowingly regarding the prohibition,
phrases.notes: He still counts as a שוגג and brings a חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ דְּיָדַע לַהּ לְשַׁבָּת בְּלָאו.
phrases.english: you can find it where he knew Shabbat as a prohibition.
phrases.notes: He knew the לאו but not the כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question of Step 9, using רבי יוחנן's definition of שגגה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: 'knowing שבת' means knowing the לאו, while being unaware of כרת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Knowing שבת while being unaware of the מלאכות seemed impossible for רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי יוחנן, he knew the לאו of the מלאכות but not their כרת, which still counts as שוגג.

steps.title: Under ריש לקיש, what did he know about שבת?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says a person is only a שוגג if he was unaware of both the לאו and the כרת. Then what part of שבת did he know?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he holds like רבי שמעון בן לקיש, who said a person is not a שוגג until he is unaware of both the לאו and the כרת, then in what way did he know שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer of Step 10 does not work under ריש לקיש, and asks again what 'knowing שבת' could mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריש לקיש, knowing the לאו makes the person a מזיד, not a שוגג. So the person must have been unaware of all the מלאכות entirely, both the לאו and the כרת. Then nothing seems left for him to 'know' about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Not until he is unaware of

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: But if he holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
who said: not until he is unaware of both the prohibition and karet,
in what way did he know Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of Step 10 only works under רבי יוחנן, not under ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 10, when applied to ריש לקיש's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under ריש לקיש, knowing the לאו makes the person a מזיד. So he must be fully unaware of the מלאכות, and there is nothing left of שבת for him to know.

steps.title: He knew the law of תחומין, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: He knew that walking past the שבת boundary (תחומין) is forbidden. רבי עקיבא holds that this is a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He knew about תחומין, according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the person's knowledge of שבת was his knowledge of תחומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that תחומין is a Torah law, but it carries only a לאו, not כרת, and it is not one of the 39 מלאכות. So the person truly 'knew שבת' through this law. Yet he was fully unaware of all the מלאכות, both their לאו and their כרת, so he is a שוגג even under ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת boundaries: the limit of how far one may walk outside a town on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבא, 'knowing שבת but not the מלאכות' means either: (1) per רבי יוחנן, he knew the לאו but not the כרת; or (2) per ריש לקיש, he knew only the Torah law of תחומין (per רבי עקיבא).
steps.confusionAlert: תחומין is not one of the 39 מלאכות and does not carry כרת. That is exactly why knowing it counts as 'knowing שבת' without knowing the מלאכות.

phrases.english: He knew about Shabbat boundaries,
and this follows Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא holds תחומין is a Torah law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a different Torah law of שבת that the person could know.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under ריש לקיש, there seemed to be nothing about שבת he could know.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knew the Torah prohibition of תחומין (per רבי עקיבא), which is a שבת law but not a מלאכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's position fits רבי יוחנן's case, and also fits ריש לקיש's case through תחומין.

steps.title: The משנה opens: 39 main מלאכות, starting with the bread-making series
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states there are 39 אבות מלאכות and lists the first 11, which follow the steps of making bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: The main categories of work are forty minus one: sowing, plowing, reaping, gathering sheaves, threshing, winnowing, selecting, grinding, sifting, kneading, and baking.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the total number of main forbidden labors on שבת and lists the first group, the bread-making steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 39 is the same number רבי יוחנן explained in Step 8: one who does all of them in one lapse of awareness brings a separate קרבן for each. These first 11 follow the order of growing grain and turning it into bread, from the field to the oven.

keyTerms.meaning: The main categories of forbidden work on שבת
Winnowing: tossing grain in the wind to separate the chaff

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up זורה (winnowing in the wind) with בורר (picking out waste). They are listed as two separate מלאכות.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The primary categories of labor are forty minus one:
one who sows, and one who plows, and one who reaps,
and one who gathers sheaves, and one who threshes, and one who winnows.
One who selects, one who grinds, and one who sifts,
and one who kneads, and one who bakes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins. It is the full list behind the number already quoted in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are 39 main forbidden labors. The first 11 are the bread-making steps, from sowing to baking.

steps.title: The cloth-making series of מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the labors involved in making clothing, from shearing wool to tearing in order to sew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shearing wool, whitening it, combing it, dyeing it, spinning, stretching the threads on the loom, making two loops, weaving two threads, cutting two threads, tying, untying, sewing two stitches, and tearing in order to sew two stitches.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list with the second group: the steps of turning wool into finished cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several of these labors come with a minimum amount, such as 'two threads' or 'two stitches.' Below that amount, a person is not liable for a קרבן. These minimums connect to the earlier discussion of mistakes about שיעורין (Step 9).

keyTerms.meaning: Combing out and straightening wool fibers
Stretching the long threads (warp) on the loom
Loops (heddles) that hold the warp threads on the loom

steps.whyThisMatters: Tearing is a מלאכה only when it is done 'in order to sew.' This shows that a destructive act can count when it serves a building purpose.

phrases.english: One who shears the wool, one who whitens it,
and one who combs it, and one who dyes it, and one who spins,
and one who stretches the warp, and one who makes two loops,
and one who weaves two threads,
and one who severs two threads.
One who ties, and one who unties,
and one who sews two stitches,
one who tears in order to sew two stitches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with the next group of labors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cloth-making labors are main מלאכות, some with set minimum amounts (two threads, two stitches).

steps.title: The hide-preparing series of מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the labors involved in preparing leather, starting from trapping an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who traps a deer, slaughters it, skins it, salts it, tans its hide, smooths it, and cuts it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the third group: the steps of turning an animal into usable leather. The list keeps going later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This series follows the order of making leather, from catching the animal to cutting the finished hide to size. The deer is just an example; trapping any living creature falls under צד.

phrases.english: One who traps a deer, one who slaughters it, and one who skins it,
one who salts it, and one who tans its hide,
and one who smooths it, and one who cuts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with the leather-making group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leather-making labors, from trapping to cutting the hide, are main מלאכות.

steps.title: The final labors: writing, building, fire, finishing, and carrying
steps.stepSummary: The משנה completes its list with writing and erasing, building and demolishing, extinguishing and kindling, the final hammer blow, and carrying from one domain to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who writes two letters, and one who erases in order to write two letters. One who builds, and one who demolishes. One who extinguishes a fire, and one who kindles a fire. One who strikes with a hammer, and one who carries something from one domain to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its list of the 39 אבות מלאכות. These last labors are not tied to bread, clothing, or leather. They are separate kinds of work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these come in pairs: writing and erasing, building and demolishing, extinguishing and kindling. Erasing and demolishing usually count only when done for a constructive purpose, which is why the משנה says erasing "in order to write." The list ends with מכה בפטיש, the last touch that completes an item, and הוצאה, moving an object from one רשות to another.

keyTerms.meaning: Writing two letters, the minimum amount that counts as writing
Erasing in order to write, meaning erasing for a constructive purpose
Extinguishing a fire and kindling a fire
Literally "striking with a hammer." It means the final finishing blow that completes an item
Carrying an object out from one domain to another

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read מכה בפטיש as only banging with a hammer. It is the category of the final finishing act that makes an item complete and usable, and the hammer blow is just the classic example.

phrases.english: One who writes two letters,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמּוֹחֵק עַל מְנָת לִכְתּוֹב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת.
phrases.english: and one who erases in order to write two letters.
phrases.notes: Erasing counts as a labor when it is done for a constructive purpose.

phrases.english: One who builds, and one who demolishes,
one who extinguishes, and one who kindles,
one who strikes with a hammer,
phrases.notes: The final blow that completes the making of an item.

phrases.english: one who carries out from domain to domain

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list after the leather group in Step 15 and gives the remaining independent labors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing, erasing in order to write, building, demolishing, extinguishing, kindling, the final hammer blow, and carrying between domains are each אבות מלאכות.

steps.title: The total: these are the 39 primary labors
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes the list by stating that all the labors it named are the אבות מלאכות, and that there are 39 of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the primary categories of labor: forty minus one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה wraps up the whole list by counting it. All the labors it named come to 39.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 opened by saying there are 39 אבות מלאכות, and this line closes the list with the same number, so the list begins and ends with the count. Saying "forty less one" instead of "thirty-nine" is the משנה's usual style for this number.

keyTerms.meaning: "These are," a phrase that sums up a list

steps.whatToRemember: The 39 אבות מלאכות fall into groups: making bread, making clothing, preparing leather, and then a final set (writing and erasing, building and demolishing, extinguishing and kindling, the final hammer blow, and carrying).
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא has already asked why the משנה needed to state the number at all, and Step 8 quotes that discussion. רבי יוחנן's answer was that the count teaches a rule: one who does many מלאכות in one lapse of awareness brings a separate חטאת for each.

phrases.english: these are the primary categories of labor
forty less one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the full list given in Steps 13 through 16 and repeats the number 39 stated at the opening.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the labors listed in the משנה together make up the 39 אבות מלאכות of שבת.
